Lead captured via self-serve signup: CTO created API key, ran smoke tests. CTO (Ravi Menon) and Lead Engineer (Sofia Alvarez) joined discovery call 2026-03-02. Primary ask: fast, easy integration into existing Vercel storefront and Next.js app; they use Typescript + Next 14 on Vercel Edge Functions. Wants pre-built adapters for LangChain (TypeScript), LlamaIndex/Node, and a Vercel AI SDK example that calls Redwood hosted_api for both chat and embeddings. Key quote: "We want an example that we can drop into our storefront and see search results in <48 hours." 

Initial findings from demo: embedding latency on Redwood test account looked promising (~45-75ms on eu-west region), chat generation latency varies by model & length; they requested guidance to keep cold-starts under 150ms for short prompts. Cost sensitivity: SMB budget; estimate target ARR <$25k first year.

Security notes: they accept public cloud but legal wants SOC2 attestation and a clear audit-log export example (how to surface token-level latency/cost per request). Also asked about retention controls and a simple KMS integration path though not mandatory for MVP.

Integration preferences and constraints (from call):
- Tech stack: Next.js + Typescript, Vercel Edge, Postgres for user metadata, Algolia currently for search.
- Wants LLM embeddings to replace Algolia vectors gradually; needs example of batch indexing pipeline and incremental refresh.
- LangChain usage: RetrievalQA pipeline; asked for a TS example using Redwood embeddings + continuous batching config.
- LlamaIndex: asked for Node connector + JSON index export for re-ingestion.
- Vercel AI SDK: wants an edge function example that streams chat responses to the client and uses Redwood hosted_api streaming tokens.
- Observability: wants per-route latency and token cost dashboard screenshots for execs (requested a one-pager).

Customer urgency: medium — runway to commit if quickstarts + sample repos arrive in 7–10 days. They want an OKR-aligned pilot to show product search relevance improvement by April proof-of-concept.
